target.title: fix: reclaim superseded reply turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users in Telegram-visible conversations could see a reply run get acknowledged or superseded, then have a previously aborted reply turn remain in the active in-memory lane and block the next visible reply for that topic.

In dogfood use this showed up as a Telegram topic appearing stuck even though the older reply run had already been aborted and no useful final answer was going to arrive from it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This updates reply-turn admission so an aborted superseded run can be reclaimed when the matching persisted run record is terminal. The reclaim stays bounded to the same session key and superseded run id, so a genuinely active reply run is still protected from accidental double admission.

The regression coverage exercises the stale aborted/superseded lane and keeps the existing active-run protection intact.

AI-assisted: yes. This was investigated and implemented through an AI-assisted local OpenClaw repair workflow, then manually re-verified with focused tests and formatting checks.

## User Impact

Telegram and other auto-reply surfaces should no longer need a manual session/topic reset for this specific stale superseded-reply lane class. A newer message can reclaim the stale aborted turn once OpenClaw can prove the old run is terminal.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto current `origin/main` at head `87434a7b80b82cdc3495120b54a7a8b9bedca9d7`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 12 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.test.ts` passed on 2 files.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- Local `codex review --base origin/main` was attempted before refreshing this PR; it started on the correct two-file diff but stalled after source-context lookup and produced no final findings, so it was stopped rather than blocking the hotfix PR.
